title: gcs-prefetch-fallback-notes
body:
Context and symptom summary:

- Intermittent model load failures seen on Dedicated pool nodes during parallel startup. Failures surface as unpack/tar errors or Python EOF/bad magic when attempting to open the weights tarball stream. Rough frequency ~1-2% of starts, higher under bursty parallel downloads.
- Hypothesis (current): optimized prefetch + concurrent range reads from GCS are occasionally producing truncated or out-of-order byte ranges under our streaming code path, leading to corrupted tar streams before checksum is validated.

Commands I tried (local reproductions + node):

1) Basic inspect of object metadata (GCS)
- gsutil stat gs://redwood-models-prod/llama-v2/weights-v1.tar.gz
- gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-models-prod/llama-v2/weights-v1.tar.gz
  -> md5Hash / crc32c reported consistently from metadata. No obvious multi-part warning.

2) Sequential vs range GETs
- Sequential download (curl):
  time curl -f -o /tmp/w.tar.gz "$(signed_url)"
  -> Works repeatedly in loop (100x) with no corruption locally.

- Range request (curl) emulating our fetcher (example):
  curl -f --header "Range: bytes=0-5242879" "$(signed_url)" -o chunk0 && curl -f --header "Range: bytes=5242880-10485759" "$(signed_url)" -o chunk1 && cat chunk* > combined.tar.gz && sha256sum combined.tar.gz
  -> On 500+ runs I saw 2 runs where tar complains: "tar: Unexpected EOF in archive"

3) Using python requests with range headers (simulating our streaming client)
- Minimal script:
  import requests
  r = requests.get(url, headers={"Range": "bytes=0-1048575"}, stream=True)
  for chunk in r.iter_content(8192): write to file

  -> Observed one run where the final size for a range chunk was smaller than expected (Content-Range header claimed full bytes).

Error snippets collected from prod nodes:

- tar: Unexpected EOF in archive
- tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
- Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runner/load_weights.py", line 342, in <module>
    stream = tarfile.open(fileobj=streaming_reader, mode="r:gz")
  File "/usr/lib/python3.10/tarfile.py", line 1620, in open
    raise ReadError("file could not be opened successfully")
  tarfile.ReadError: file could not be opened successfully

- EOFError: Ran out of input while decoding compressed chunk
- ChecksumMismatch: expected sha256=abc123, got sha256=def456

Observations / telemetry:

- Failures correlate with high parallel boot activity (many models starting in same rack).
- When a failure happens, gsutil ls -L immediately after still shows consistent metadata (md5/crc32c unchanged).
- Node-level logs show our prefetcher requested overlapping ranges (bug?) in one trace.
- Network retransmits increased on affected nodes; moderate packet drops reported by NIC driver (ixgbe) in same timeframe.

Hypotheses (ranked):

1) Race in prefetcher combining ranges: malformed queue leads to duplicate/overlap and our reassembly code appends chunks in wrong order under a concurrency window. (High likelihood)
2) GCS service returning 200 with chunk smaller than requested (headers lie) under transient error. (Medium)
3) Underlying network (NIC) drops cause TCP to reset mid-stream yielding truncated read that we don't detect until tar extraction. (Medium)
4) Object uploaded as composite by producer (parallel composite upload) makes range reads tricky. (Low)

What I tried to validate hypotheses:

- Added extra assertions in reassembly: verify each range's Content-Range header matches requested bytes before writing. Reproduced one failure where server claimed full length but body smaller. Saved raw response for analysis.
- Added ordering checks (sequence numbers) on prefetched chunks; found one case where two concurrent requests completed out of order and our reassembly appended earlier chunk after later chunk due to lock ordering bug. Fix: ensure single writer with ordered commit.
- Forced sequential single-connection download in controlled runs — no corruption observed across 200 runs.
- Instrumented http client to compare crc32c of each chunk against computed value where GCS provides component crc; not always available.

Short-term mitigations implemented on a canary pool:

- Fallback: If any range read returns smaller bytes than requested, abort and fallback to single-stream full download. (Implemented: patch #4521)
- Lock reassembly properly: ensure chunk offsets are applied deterministically. (Implemented as hotfix)
- Add per-range timeout/backoff when retries exceed 2 -> escalate to sequential download.

Longer term ideas / engineering tasks:

- Add a streaming-level checksum verification (rolling sha256) so we can detect corruption before tar extraction. (Ticketed INFR-398)
- Replace our naive range-reassembly with a small state machine that keeps ordering, validates Content-Range, validates per-chunk length, and supports hole-detection.
- Consider switching to GCS XML API for byte-range reads in critical path if JSON API is flaky (need to benchmark).
- Add producer-side guard: upload with non-composite single-object or ensure object metadata contains component checksums for per-range validation.

Reproduction plan to narrow down root cause:

1) Local lab: run N parallel curl range clients against an instrumented GCS test object (10GB) from same region as prod; vary concurrency and chunk size; capture raw responses and headers.
2) Simulate NIC drop: use tc/netem to inject packet loss and see if our client sees truncated responses where metadata still says full length.
3) Small server-side test: upload both composite and single-part versions of the same file and run identical range tests; compare behavior.

Notes to self / next steps:

- Follow up with storage infra to confirm no known incidents in the time windows (Ravi).
- Add a light E2E test into CI: start 10 parallel model-downloads on a small VM pool and assert checksum after reassembly.
- Clean up saved raw responses in /tmp/debug/gcs-prefetch/ and attach to JIRA.

Quick checklist before leaving:

- [x] Hotfix ordering lock merged (canary deployed)
- [x] Fallback to sequential on partial chunk implemented
- [ ] Add rolling checksum detection prototype (next week)
- [ ] Run controlled repro at scale (need 3 spare nodes)

Misc notes / random log excerpt (kept verbatim):

-- raw response capture 2024-02-23T03:12:17Z --
HTTP/2 200
content-range: bytes 5242880-10485759/42949672960
content-length: 5242877

(body length 5242877 bytes, expected 5242880)

Conclusion (working hypothesis):

Most failures are caused by our concurrent range-prefetch + reassembly path having ordering/length-validation bugs. There's also evidence that on rare occasions GCS or the network returns fewer bytes than requested while still reporting content-range header claim; to be safe, we should validate per-chunk lengths and prefer single-stream downloads as fallback.

If this reproduces in lab we can close as client bug; if failure persists with sequential download, escalate to storage provider with reproducible raw captures attached.

--- end of notes ---
